analysis.subject: physics
analysis.pageCoverage: Page indexes fundamentals of motion and aerodynamics, Wright aircraft from 1900 to 1905 including gliders and powered flyers, plus interactive simulations for elevators, wind tunnel tests and performance predictions.

overview.headline: Wright flight fundamentals, aerodynamics lessons and aircraft simulations overview

keyPoints.point: Fundamentals and lessons are presented to help understand the journey of flight.
keyPoints.quote: These fundamentals and lessons will help you understand their journey of flight.

keyPoints.point: The collection shows basic math and physics that led to invention of the airplane.
keyPoints.quote: The Wright Way will show you the basic math and physics that led to the invention of the airplane by the Wright Brothers.

keyPoints.point: Elevators are found at the front of the aircraft as movable control surfaces.
keyPoints.quote: At the front of all of the Wright brothers’ aircraft one finds the elevators.

keyPoints.point: The machine is described as the first piloted aircraft that was heavier than air.
keyPoints.quote: This machine was the first piloted aircraft that was heavier than air, ...

keyTerms.gloss: Laws that describe motion of bodies under forces, central to flight analysis
measure of turning effect described as Moments about an axis
thin Boundary region near a wing surface where air flow is slowed by viscosity
Bernoulli relation linking pressure and velocity for steady fluid flow along a streamline
Lift force generated by wings that opposes weight to sustain flight

componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Tracing glider to powered aircraft in page order helps learners see design progression from early tests to first flights.
Fact recall about lift, weight and first flight details reinforces core aerodynamics vocabulary from descriptive sentences.
componentPlan.focusQuote: The objective of this simulation is to find the flight conditions that produce an aircraft lift greater than the aircraft weight.
